macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks retreated from records after weak consumer data
items.summary: U.S. equities fell on August 14 after surprise declines in consumer spending and sentiment raised concerns that the economy may be slowing faster than expected. The Dow fell about 108 points, the S&P 500 lost 0.2%, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.3% after the S&P had hit a record the prior day.

items.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow all closed higher on the prior session as inflation data supported Fed patience
items.summary: On August 13, the S&P 500 set a record close, the Nasdaq gained 0.81%, and the Dow rose 0.13% as tame producer-price inflation reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would not raise rates at its September meeting.

items.title: Inflation eased in July, but remained above the Fed's target
items.summary: U.S. consumer prices rose 3.4% year over year in July, down from 3.5% in June, indicating inflation is cooling but still not low enough to eliminate rate-hike concerns. Reuters and the BBC said lower food and gasoline costs helped ease prices, while housing kept inflation elevated.

items.title: Retail sales fell sharply in July, signaling weaker consumer spending
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. retail sales declined in July for the first time in nine months, and CNN said the drop was 0.6%, the steepest since May 2025. Economists cut third-quarter growth estimates after the weaker spending data.

items.title: Wholesale inflation slowed more than expected
items.summary: CNN Business reported that U.S. wholesale inflation eased in July more than economists expected, adding to signs that price pressures are gradually moderating. The data was viewed as supportive of the view that the Fed can remain on hold in September.

items.title: Fed rate-hike odds shifted after soft inflation and weaker retail data
items.summary: United Daily News said traders increased the probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged in September to nearly 70%, up from 56% a week earlier, after weaker jobs, inflation, and retail readings. MarketWatch also noted that a tame inflation report could help the Fed avoid further tightening soon.

items.title: Oil and geopolitical risks remained a focus for markets
items.summary: Market commentary highlighted ongoing volatility tied to the Strait of Hormuz and tensions around the U.S.-Iran standoff, with oil price moves affecting equity sentiment. One report said falling oil prices recently eased pressure on U.S. stocks, while another noted commodity markets were still reacting to deadlock around the Strait.

items.title: Large-cap tech remained a driver of U.S. market gains
items.summary: The August 13 rally was led by heavyweight technology shares, with the Nasdaq outperforming as investors continued to favor mega-cap growth stocks. The cited market coverage did not identify a single dominant earnings release, but it emphasized tech strength as the main contributor to index gains.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $63,000 as regulatory delay and selling pressure weigh on crypto
items.summary: Bitcoin traded slightly below $63,000 and was roughly flat over 24 hours, with selling pressure and delayed U.S. regulatory action offsetting broader equity strength. Ether rose modestly, while XRP slipped slightly.

items.title: SEC postpones planned innovation exemption for tokenization projects
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission delayed a planned innovation exemption for tokenization projects, extending uncertainty around when blockchain-based financial products may receive regulatory relief. The report also notes preliminary conditional approval for World Liberty Trust Company to operate as a national trust bank.

items.title: Crypto derivatives see about $49.2 million in liquidations over 24 hours
items.summary: Across crypto futures markets, total liquidations reached about $49.2 million in the past day, according to market data cited by KuCoin. Bitcoin liquidations were the largest share among major assets listed in the report.

items.title: Bitcoin developers use AI tools to uncover nearly 5,000 security vulnerabilities
items.summary: Forbes reported that Bitcoin developers used AI tools to identify almost 5,000 security vulnerabilities across nearly 400 projects in 24 hours. The item highlights continued security tooling development in the broader blockchain ecosystem.

items.title: Ripple Swell 2026 draws 75+ speakers and 1,500+ expected attendees
items.summary: Ripple confirmed more than 75 speakers for Swell 2026 and said it expects over 1,500 attendees. The event update signals continued ecosystem activity around XRP and enterprise blockchain adoption.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 3.7 Flash
items.summary: Reports indicate Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after its previous model update, with improvements in coding and agent capabilities. This points to an accelerated release cadence among frontier AI labs.

items.title: Anthropic adds invisible watermarks to Claude outputs
items.summary: Anthropic’s Claude is reportedly adding invisible watermarks to text and image outputs. The change appears aimed at attribution and provenance as AI-generated content becomes harder to distinguish from human work.

items.title: DeepSeek V4-Pro-0813 boosts agent capabilities
items.summary: DeepSeek said its V4-Pro-0813 update substantially improves agent performance and is available through API, app, and web access. The release adds to the growing competition from Chinese AI model makers.

items.title: Alibaba's Qwen models surpass 3 billion downloads
items.summary: Alibaba’s Qwen family has reportedly crossed 3 billion downloads, overtaking Meta and Google in cumulative usage. The milestone underscores the scale and momentum of Chinese open model ecosystems.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic face pricing pressure as rivals gain ground
items.summary: Coverage says OpenAI and Anthropic are cutting prices amid increased competition from cheaper Chinese AI models. The trend suggests pressure on premium frontier-model pricing and margins.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Senate opens child-safety investigation into Roblox
items.summary: A U.S. Senate subcommittee has launched an investigation into Roblox, with senators saying the platform may prioritize revenue and engagement over child safety. The move increases regulatory pressure on the company after allegations of criminal activity on the platform.

items.title: Netflix shuts down two game studios
items.summary: Netflix is closing two of its gaming studios, including Night School Studio, despite the acclaim around its work on Unhinged. The closures add to signs of tightening investment and restructuring in Netflix’s games push.

items.title: Nintendo’s next Fire Emblem gets a new structure and September release date
items.summary: Nintendo has revealed a new Fire Emblem entry called Fortune’s Weave, which launches on September 17. The announcement signals a major upcoming first-party release for Switch players.

items.title: Sonic Frontiers surpasses 5 million copies sold
items.summary: SEGA announced that Sonic Frontiers has officially sold more than 5 million copies. The milestone highlights continued commercial strength for one of SEGA’s biggest recent releases.

items.title: Kingdom Hearts IV gets a late-2027 release window and new series announcement
items.summary: Coverage in Japanese gaming news reports that Kingdom Hearts IV is now slated for release in the second half of 2027. The same reports also mention a new animated Kingdom Hearts series being announced for Disney+.

items.title: Fortnite Sonic comic teases new crossover skins and content
items.summary: Beebom reports that Fortnite released a Sonic-themed comic and is teasing four new skins for Season 4. The update adds to Fortnite’s ongoing crossover-heavy content strategy.

items.title: Battlefield 6 free trial and Top Gun collaboration announced
items.summary: Beebom reports that Battlefield 6 will be free to try next week and will include a Top Gun collaboration. The promotion suggests a marketing push aimed at bringing lapsed and new players into the game.

items.title: Game of Thrones: War for Westeros gameplay reveal set for Gamescom
items.summary: Beebom reports that the first gameplay reveal for Game of Thrones: War for Westeros has been announced for Gamescom Opening Night Live. The reveal will give players their first substantial look at the project.

items.title: Helldivers 2 arrives in PlayStation Plus Game Catalog for SEA players
items.summary: Explosion reports that Helldivers 2 has been added to the PS Plus Game Catalog for Southeast Asia. The inclusion expands access to one of Sony’s recent high-profile live-service releases.

items.title: Marathon’s Vault Breaker PvE mode ends August 18
items.summary: Explosion reports that Marathon’s Vault Breaker PvE mode is scheduled to end on August 18. The timing points to another notable live-service update around Bungie’s shooter.
